question.problem:
The following table shows some values of a continuous function $f(x)$ over the interval $[0,8].$

| $x$ | $0$ | $2$ | $5$ | $6$ | $8$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $3$ | $4$ | $6$ | $5$ | $9$ |

Use the left Riemann sum, with the four subintervals indicated by the data, to approximate the area $A$ under the curve $y=f(x)$ over the interval $[0,8].$ 

$A≈$ 
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
In this case, we have $n=4$ rectangles. Using the left Riemann sum, the area is approximated as

$$
A≈f(0)Δ{x}_{1}+f(2)Δ{x}_{2}+f(5)Δ{x}_{3}+f(6)Δ{x}_{4},
$$

where each $Δ{x}_{i}$ is calculated by considering the step between a particular $x$-value and the next one, i.e.,

$$
Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i+1}-{x}_{i}.
$$

We set up a value table that includes the $Δx$'s.

| $x$ | $0$ | $2$ | $5$ | $6$ | $8$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $Δx$ | $2$ | $3$ | $1$ | $2$ | $-$ |
| $f(x)$ | $3$ | $4$ | $6$ | $5$ | $9$ |

Finally, we plug in the numbers to approximate the area under the curve and get

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈3\cdot 2+4\cdot 3+6\cdot 1+5\cdot 2 \\  & =6+12+6+10 \\  & =34.\end{aligned}
$$
